pages.name: Vienna: Smyslov, 3...Bc5 4.Bg2 Nc6
pages.notes: Plan 2 named d4/e4 as 'key central squares', which the parser read as moves; rewrote it with the standard ideas (...a6 against Na4, ...Nd4, ...Be6/...Qd7/...Bh3 to trade the g2-bishop).

pages.name: King's Gambit Accepted: Bishop's Gambit, Kieseritzky Gambit
pages.notes: Plan 2 put White's Bxb5 in Black's plan; rewrote it as ...Nf6 hitting e4 and ...c6 gaining time on the b5-bishop, then ...d5 (the first rewrite gave the tempo to ...Nf6 and the reviewer rejected it).

pages.name: King's Gambit Accepted: Allgaier, Urusov Attack
pages.notes: Plan 3 routed the king ...Kh7-g8 when it stands on g7; rewrote it (king on g7/h7, give back material). Plan 1 now adds Bxf4 to win back material. British spelling in plan 4.

pages.name: King's Knight Opening: Gunderam Gambit, Bishop Attack
pages.notes: Plan 4 suggested ...Nc6 and ...O-O-O, impossible with the pawn on c6 and Black's king headed short; rewrote it around the ...Bxc3+ and ...Qxc3 threat, then ...O-O, ...d5, ...Nbd7. British spelling in plan 2.

pages.name: King's Pawn Game: Gunderam Gambit
pages.notes: Plan 3 had Re1 before White can castle; rewrote it as the immediate Nxe5 (e5 is undefended after 2...c6). British spelling in the overview and plans 1, 2 and 4.

pages.name: Latvian Gambit Accepted: Bronstein Gambit
pages.notes: The overview said Black sacrifices material; it is White who leaves d4 unguarded after Qh5+ g6 Qe2, with material level. Rewrote it; plan 3 had O-O/Re1 with the f1-bishop at home; plans 1 and 2 got Nc3/Be3 and a half-open (not open) f-file.

pages.name: Latvian Gambit Accepted: Nimzowitsch Attack
pages.notes: Plan 1 named 'squares like d5 and f5', read as moves; rewrote it around Nc3 hitting e4, Be2 and O-O, the e3-knight on d5/g4. Plan 2 had both ...c6 and ...Nc6 and an 'open' f-file (half-open).

pages.name: Latvian Gambit: 3.d4 fxe4 5.Nxe5 Nf6
pages.notes: Plan 1 named 'the weak f7 and e6 squares' (f7 read as a pawn); rewrote it around Bc4/Bg5, Nc3, pressure on e4 and the a2-g8 diagonal. British spelling in the overview and plan 3.

pages.name: Latvian Gambit: 3.Nxe5 Qf6 4.d4 d6 5.Nc4 fxe4
pages.notes: Plan 2 had a Nc3-e3 route for a knight on c4; rewrote it as Nc3 and Ne3. Plan 1 called the line a pawn sacrifice when material is level. British spelling in the overview and plan 4.

pages.name: Latvian Gambit: Corkscrew Countergambit
pages.notes: Plan 1 targeted an f7-pawn that is gone; rewrote it around 5.Nf7 Qe7 6.Nxh8 d5 and Bf7+. Plan 2 claimed a White material advantage when material is level; plan 3 said 'open' f-file (half-open) and now notes ...d5 hits c4.
